quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do to turn right at a red light?

options.text: Slow down and check for traffic before turning.
Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Check for signs that prohibit the turn.
Signal and wait until the light turns green.
Wait for a green turn arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Check for signs that prohibit the turn.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you may turn right if no sign says you cannot. You must come to a full stop first. Always signal before you turn.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the middle of a road mean?

options.text: Traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic is moving in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic is moving in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop on the road at night?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use only your parking lights.
Use only your headlights.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think children are done getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Do not move until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect tires that are in good condition.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on wet roads, your tires cannot remove water as well. If you go too fast, your tires may lose grip and hydroplane, causing you to slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: How much alcohol does your body eliminate each hour?

options.text: Half a drink.
One drink.
Two drinks.
Three drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour.

questions.question: When you enter a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so traffic and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and make sure no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. You must stop before you reach the sidewalk area.

questions.question: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What should you always do at a light rail intersection?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and cyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all signs and signals. Trains share the road with cars, pedestrians, and cyclists.

questions.question: When can you park on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: Anytime you have your emergency flashers on.
If your vehicle is not on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: To park legally on a street, your vehicle must be within:

options.text: Six inches of the curb.
12 inches of the curb.
18 inches of the curb.
24 inches of the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: You cannot park more than 12 inches away from the curb on a street.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Turning on your car radio.
Slowing down.
Stopping at regular intervals to rest.
Moving your eyes from side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping at regular intervals to rest.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly on long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to your previous lane.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light allows you to drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may turn right or left on green unless a sign prohibits it. Yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash along the highway ahead.
Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are at play ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or very close to the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: A driver age 21 or older may not operate a vehicle if they have ____ nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood.

options.text: Zero
One
Three
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Five
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot drive with five or more nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood. Drivers under 21 cannot drive with any THC in their blood. Driving under the influence of marijuana is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not permitted.
Left turns are permitted.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not permitted.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest thing to do is:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: Driving while under the influence of marijuana is:

options.text: Legal.
Illegal.
Legal, but not recommended.
Recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of marijuana is illegal, even if the marijuana is used legally. It distorts your sense of space, time, and speed, making driving dangerous.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires all three conditions: clear visibility ahead, enough space to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle capable of passing speed. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop immediately and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what should you do first to slow down?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first release the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Drive onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist when it is safe. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed. You can only cross these lines to turn into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction. You can only cross these lines to turn or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the other lane is clear and safe.
